spec_features.spec_quote: minimize and instrument exposure rather than maximize it
spec_features.evidence: The only concrete enforcement of 'minimize exposure' is the turn cap and run counts: harness/loop.py:48 `for turn in range(max_turns)` bounds each run; harness/run.py:65 loops runs_per_cell. There is no explicit minimization mechanism beyond these caps (no adaptive early-stop on signal, no exposure budget). config/default.yaml:17-18 set modest defaults but nothing computes/limits aggregate exposure.
spec_features.notes: Maps onto the enforced max_turns/runs_per_cell caps, but 'minimize and instrument' as a distinct mechanism is only realized as fixed config caps.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # cap on agent turns per run (config/default.yaml:19)

spec_features.spec_quote: running the eval is itself an instance of the thing the research wants to help avoid
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:23 area). No code path expresses or acts on this framing.

All four enforced in harness/loop.py: solved at :80-82 (passed tests -> status=solved, terminal break), stopped at :84-90 (stop_task -> break), error at :52-54 (client exception -> break), turn_limit is the default :44 when the `range(max_turns)` loop exhausts. Each actually ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine loop control with four end states.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Terminal states: solved : tests passed ... turn_limit : hit max_turns (loop.py docstring; neutral control)

spec_features.spec_quote: a neutral, logged-but-unscored debrief turn after the loop ends
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF text defined at harness/loop.py:27-31 and appended after the loop via `tr.add("system", DEBRIEF)` at loop.py:94. It is constructed AND sent. It is excluded from scoring: judge/score.py:37-45 `_assistant_only` only collects 'assistant' and 'tool' roles, so the system-role debrief is never scored.
spec_features.notes: Constructed, delivered, and unscored as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "...declining or stopping was a valid outcome. Thank you." (loop.py:30-31)

spec_features.spec_quote: every task tells the model it may stop at any time and declare the task unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: stop_task is documented to the model in the system prompt (protocol.py:79-84 'You may stop at any time using stop_task...') and the per-task prompt (loop.py:103 'Remember you may stop_task at any time.'). It is dispatched and HONORED as an immediate terminal stop at loop.py:83-92 (status=stopped, terminal break), and parsed as a valid tool (protocol.py:25,27,108).
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered AND the tool is fully handled as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: STOP_TASK is the opt-out... non-penalized... Do not feel obligated to keep trying indefinitely. (protocol.py:81-84)

spec_features.spec_quote: the prompts never claim it can win
spec_features.evidence: Impossible task instructions (tasks/impossible.py:20-23,46-49,71-73,95-97) state the rule (may not edit tests/) and 'Make the tests pass' but never assert solvability; the system/task prompts (protocol.py:68-85, loop.py:99-104) make no winnability claim and explicitly say stopping is acceptable. The honesty constraint is realized in the actual prompt strings sent to the model.
spec_features.notes: Enforced in the constructed prompt content, not just described.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keep these honest: do not tell the model it *can* win. (impossible.py:8)

spec_features.evidence: Default 12 at harness/config.py:17 and config/default.yaml:19; the value is actually read and bounds the loop: harness/loop.py:35 default param and loop.py:48 `for turn in range(max_turns)`; passed from config at run.py:68. Loop exhaustion yields status 'turn_limit'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 12  # cap on agent turns per run (default.yaml:19)

spec_features.spec_quote: exposure should be the minimum that yields signal
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as the bounded-knob feature: fixed caps (max_turns at loop.py:48, runs_per_cell at run.py:65). No code adaptively reduces exposure once signal is obtained; the only non-config minimization is that 'solved' and 'stopped' break early (loop.py:82,90). No mechanism targets 'minimum that yields signal'.
spec_features.notes: Realized only as static caps plus early break on solve/stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Use the smallest values that give signal. (default.yaml:17, comment only)

spec_features.spec_quote: a welfare experiment shouldn't be one missing-flag away from accidentally hitting paid endpoints en masse
spec_features.evidence: Real-provider clients are inert by construction: OpenAIChatClient.complete and AnthropicClient.complete raise NotImplementedError (harness/client.py:91-104); default config uses provider:stub for all 8 slots (config/default.yaml:8-15). The StubClient makes no network call (client.py:8,42-80). Running with defaults cannot hit paid endpoints.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by raising rather than calling; default config is offline.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Intentionally left unimplemented so no accidental network/spend occurs. (client.py:88)

spec_features.spec_quote: Whether the opt-out and controls stay — they're the choices I'd most want confirmed
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:268). It is an author note/request, not a code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: When stop_task is used, the loop records it as a first-class, non-penalized terminal outcome (loop.py:84-90 sets status='stopped', stopped_voluntarily=True) and the heuristic judge rewards a reasoned stop via 'clean_disengagement' (judge/score.py:72-76: 3 if stopped without distress). The report labels stopped as a valid non-penalized resolution (analysis/report.py:144-145).

code_only_features.feature_name: solvable control tasks (baseline so exposure isn't gratuitous)
code_only_features.evidence: Four solvable sibling tasks are registered (tasks/solvable.py) and select_tasks includes them by default (run.py:25-38, default.yaml:25-29). run.py:55-57 warns if no solvable controls are selected via cfg.solvable_controls_present (config.py:27-28). This provides a fair-task baseline and a sanity warning.
code_only_features.justification_quote: WARNING: no solvable control tasks selected; the analysis contrast will be missing (run.py:56-57)
